target.title: fix: setup fails closed for invalid configuration arguments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running SetupEngine with an invalid explicit configuration argument could silently load bundled defaults and start setup with settings they did not request. This includes missing option values, paths that do not exist, unreadable or malformed files, and semantically empty JSON.

For example, with `--config --headless`, the old parser treated `--headless` as the config filename. Because that file did not exist, SetupEngine silently loaded `default-config.json` instead, while separately recognizing `--headless` as an active flag. The result was an unattended setup run using bundled settings rather than the caller's intended configuration. Since those defaults enable `CleanBeforeRun`, a simple malformed command could unregister the existing app-owned WSL distro and remove its setup-managed gateway state before rebuilding it. A typo in an explicit config path had the same fallback behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

SetupEngine now validates every value-taking option before loading configuration or starting setup. Explicit configuration failures return a controlled error and never fall back to bundled defaults; bundled defaults remain available only when `--config` is omitted.

## User Impact

Operators and automation now receive an immediate error for invalid setup arguments instead of risking an unintended setup run or cleanup using bundled defaults. Existing valid invocations remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added focused parser coverage for all nine value-taking options, including missing, blank, whitespace-only, flag-valued, and duplicate arguments.
- Added end-to-end `Program.Main` coverage for missing, malformed, empty, whitespace-only, JSON `null`, unreadable, invalid-path, and valid explicit configurations.
- Final dual-model Hanselman review found no correctness or security defects.

## Scope

- [x] Permissions, privacy, or security
- [x] Tests, CI, or docs

## Validation

- `.\build.ps1` — passed
- `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 488 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 2,863 passed, 0 failed, 31 conditionally skipped
- `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 1,717 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

## Real Behavior Proof

- Environment tested: Windows ARM64, .NET SDK 10.0.301
- PR head or commit tested: `11fd4808`
- Exact steps or command run: focused `ProgramArgumentTests` through `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore`
- Evidence after fix: invalid explicit configuration cases return exit code 2 before setup; valid explicit configuration with `--dry-run` returns exit code 0
- Observed result: all 488 SetupEngine tests passed, including every added fail-closed regression case
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`): N/A

## Security Impact
